identity.name: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
synonyms: Mono- and diglycerides of edible fatty acids
identity.chemical_class: Mixture of glycerol mono- and di-esters of long-chain fatty acids

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic glycerides reduce oil-water interfacial tension and stabilize emulsions; they also modify texture and processing behavior.
common_food_categories: infant formula and specialized infant formula
miscellaneous processed foods using emulsifier systems

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 concluded no need for a numerical ADI; 2021 follow-up maintained no safety concern for authorized uses including infant categories with specification updates.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA found no safety concern for E471 at reported/authorized uses, but recommended tighter impurity limits (toxic elements, 3-MCPD, glycidyl esters, erucic acid).

concerns.summary: Recent mouse studies reported metabolic and microbiota effects for dietary emulsifiers including mono-/diglyceride-related systems, but evidence is heterogeneous and not directly equivalent to full E471 regulatory datasets.

EFSA follow-up identified impurity-specification concerns (toxic elements, 3-MCPD, glycidyl esters, erucic acid), indicating risk management focus on contaminant limits rather than core E471 toxicity at authorized use levels.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no numerical ADI needed and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.
EFSA 2021: no reason for a safety concern for authorized infant uses.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numerical ADI is not set (EFSA) and JECFA ADI is not limited; classical ADI exceedance is not the primary concern. Risk focus is on impurity control.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators continue to approve E471/INS471 with no numerical ADI and no core toxicological safety concern at authorized uses, but impurity-control recommendations and mixed animal microbiome findings support a limited (not risk_free) classification.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 no numerical ADI and no safety concern
EFSA 2021 infant follow-up no safety concern but tighter impurity limits requested
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR 184.1505 with cGMP conditions
No IARC listing identified for E471
Recent animal microbiome findings are mixed and indirect for E471
